overview:
The *Tikkunei Zohar* says that when G-d leaves the vessels they are left like a body without a soul. But if a vessel is made from the thickening of the light, how can it be there without the light? Because, as chapter 29 showed, the root of the vessels, in the *reshimu*, comes before the root of the lights: the vessels exist on their own, and G-d is one with them because He chose them. So in prayer one can aim at the source of the vessel, and the light follows. Rabbi Walters sets this beside the other ways of *kavana*, and says the main one is still to *daven* like a little kid.

Every vessel has an inner, a middle and an outer level, for intellect, emotion and action, and the outer one hides the most. He shows it in a man's kindness, in the heart, in the liver, in the exile, and in the *mitzvos*: *kavana*, feeling and deed, made to grow by doing them only because G-d wants it. Yet the vessels are there for the light; without it they are a body without a soul.

terms.gloss: a body without a soul: the vessels, brain, heart and liver, once the lights leave them
thickening: the lowest level of the light, brought down, makes the form of the vessel
He and His organs are one: the vessels come straight from G-d's choice, even before the lights
the middle: the middle vessel, between the inner (pnimiyus) and the outer (chitzoniyus), which limits the emotions of the light
head, middle and end: the three levels of the vessels; read backwards their initials spell seser, hidden
the vessels that bring the light out to someone else, as against the vessels that reveal it to oneself
garments: thought, speech and action, which change like clothes; below the vessels and already separate from G-dliness
the impression of life: what is left in the liver in sleep, the source of dreams; in exile, all that is seen of G-d's running of the world
pregnancy: the Jewish people in exile, like a fetus with its head folded between its knees
the kindnesses that make the body grow: the general G-dly light of every mitzva, doing what G-d wants
yichud, bracha, kedusha: the kavana, blessing and deed of a mitzva; also the name of a river

sections.title: The vessels exist on their own: a body without a soul
sections.summary: The *Tikkunei Zohar* says that vessels the light has left are like a body without a soul. Since a vessel is made from the thickening of the light, that raises a question; the answer is that the root of the vessels comes before the root of the lights, so the vessels have an existence of their own and come straight from G-d's choice.

blocks.text:
The last three chapters explained lights and vessels. When the *or* (light) comes into the *kli* (vessel), it changes from spiritual to physical, and it also becomes limited. That is the general idea of lights and vessels.

Then, for a more particular *hisbonenus* (contemplation), came the idea of *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: G-d is one both with the lights and with the vessels, because He decides what the limitation is going to be and what the vessel is going to be. That comes from His *bechira* (choice), just as the lights do. The lights are revealed as simple and infinite and the vessels as limited, but since the limitation comes from His choice, it too is really one with Him: its only existence is G-d's choice.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.title: A cup for the water
blocks.text: It was also explained that the vessels come from the *hisabus* (thickening) of the light: when the light is to be brought down, its lowest level makes the form of the vessel. A person wants to drink water, and water is liquidy; he cannot really hold it in his hand. So he comes up with the idea of a cup, and from that desire comes the form of the cup: it has to be waterproof, and it has to be able to hold the water. Or the power of sight: the eye has to be made in a way that it can see. That is how the thickening of the light makes the vessel.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Now we can understand the saying of the *Tikkunei Zohar*, in *Pasach Eliyahu*, which we say every week: when You leave them, the vessels, the names, they are left *gufa b'lo nishmasa*, like a body without a soul. The body is **the vessels of the brain, the heart, and the liver**, and the soul is the *oros* (lights) of *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*.

blocks.question: The previous chapter explained that the vessel is created by the thickening of the light. If the vessel is made out of the light, how can it be there once the light leaves it?
blocks.text: Based on what the previous chapter explained, **the source of the vessels precedes the source of the lights**: the vessels come from the *reshimu* (impression), which is before the *Kav* (the ray of light). The *reshimu* is the source of the vessels, and the *Kav* is the source of the lights. If so, the vessels have their existence independent of the light. They really exist on their own.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: And about this it says *ihu v'garmohi chad*: **G-d is one with His organs, He is one with the vessels**. The lights and the vessels both originally come from the *etzem* (essence), from G-d's essence: He chooses the lights and He chooses the vessels. And the source of the vessels is actually revealed before the lights, in the *reshimu*; only afterwards are the lights revealed. So the vessels come straight from the essence, without needing the light in between.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: This is the idea of the matter of the vessel, which comes before the light. The light only makes the form of the vessel; the actual vessel itself comes from before that. And the truth is that even the form of the vessel exists without the light. The light is just choosing which form it should take on.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.title: The body does not turn back into dirt
blocks.text: The soul controls the body and helps it develop in a certain form, but when the soul leaves, the body does not immediately lose its form. So you can have a body without a soul. It does not immediately turn back into dirt, because it has a certain existence without the soul.

sections.title: Aiming at the source of the vessel, and praying like a little kid
sections.summary: So one who is *mechaven* in the Name should aim at the source that creates the vessel, and the light follows by itself. Rabbi Walters sets the ways of *kavana* of chapters 28 to 30 side by side, and says the main one is still the simple prayer of a child, who pictures G-d and does not limit Him.

phrases.en: Based on this,

phrases.en: when you're *davening* and you're *mechaven* to the names,

phrases.en: because it's the way of a man *lachazor achar isha*, to go after a woman.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Based on this, when you are *davening* and you are *mechaven* (directing your intention) to the names, **you should be *mechaven* to the source that creates the *kli***. That is the main thing of the name, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: that G-d chooses the vessels, that He chooses how they should be. That is why they represent Him, why they are a name.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: And automatically, if you recognize that G-d is choosing how the vessel should be, it reveals Him, and the light is drawn down by itself, "because it's the way of a man *lachazor achar isha*, to go after a woman." When you have the *kli*, which is like the woman, the *or*, which is like the man, will automatically come. *V'dai l'mevin* (and this is enough for one who understands).

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text:
So far these chapters have explained ways to *daven*. Chapter 28 said to be *mechaven* to the lights, to the source of the lights, and automatically one is *mechaven* to the vessel as well. Chapter 29 said to be *mechaven* to the vessels, the external vessels, and automatically one is *mechaven* to their source. And here it says to be *mechaven* to the source of the vessels, and automatically the light comes too.

Notice that in this chapter and in chapter 28, where he explains what to be *mechaven* to, it is in parentheses, and in chapter 29 it is not. That is because chapter 29 is the simple *pshat* (plain meaning) of how you should *daven*.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text:
You should *daven* like a little kid: ask G-d for what you want, in the vessel that you want. "Please give me food and health and things like that," and you are *mechaven* that G-d is the one who gives you food and health, which is the external vessel.

Then there is a higher way of *davening*, *mechaven* to the light: what you really want is not the food and the health and the money, but that there should be *gilui Elokus* (a revelation of G-dliness), which is the light. And if you try to have the light, you become a *kli* and a *merkava* (chariot) to G-dliness, and automatically you will get everything good *b'gashmiyus* (materially) too.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: And here he is saying: when you are *mechaven* to the source of the vessel, that G-d really can do anything, then although He could make it come out any way, you are asking Him to make it come out this way, and you are recognizing that this is a revelation of Him. So automatically that brings out the light. Here too you want G-d to be revealed in a tangible way, and that is why you want it to come into a vessel. This is another, higher way of *davening*.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: These two ways in parentheses are a deeper type of *kavana*, a higher way of *davening*. Nevertheless, the main *kavana* should be as he says in chapter 29, not in the parentheses: you should *daven* like a kid, *al daas zeh hatinok*. The Rebbe said this about himself, and it says so in the *Gemara* too: "I pray with the mind of this little child," the way this little kid *davens*. And really, if you *daven* like that, you automatically have all these other *kavanos*.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: In the simple way a kid *davens*, the deeper type of *davening* is really hidden. A little kid thinks about G-d, and even if he thinks about Him in a vessel and pictures Him as an invisible guy with a long white beard or something, he does not really think that G-d is a person. He does not limit Him. When it says G-d took us out of Egypt with His arm, with a *yad rama* or a *yad chazaka* (an uplifted or a strong hand), he pictures G-d picking us up with a physical hand and taking us out. But even though he is picturing a physical thing, the kid does not think that G-d is limited to that, to a body. He thinks G-d can do whatever He wants, "it's magic": He made Himself like that, or He decided to do it like this, but it does not limit Him.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: An adult, even when he is picturing the highest thing, the best thing he can picture is something like *Adam Kadmon*, but he thinks he really understands what G-d is, so he really limits Him to that. And if you really limit G-d even to *Adam Kadmon*, it already says that it is so close to *avoda zara* (idol worship) that you can already call it *avoda zara*. While the way a little kid thinks of G-d is so close to the truth that you can *mamash* call it the truth.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Nevertheless, we should be aware of these different types of *davening*. This is the thing that the *Arizal* said: be *mechaven* to the light within the *sefiros*, not to the vessels. The *Baal Shem Tov* said: be *mechaven* to the G-dliness within the *sefiros*, not just to the light. And the *Alter Rebbe* said, "But I say that you should be *mechaven* to the *Atzmus*" (G-d's essence). Once you are like that, you have everything. That is like a little kid: to be *mechaven* to the essence is the main thing.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: But in the back of your mind you should learn how it works with lights and vessels, and understand how these things are a *gilui Elokus*, how the light is and how the vessel is, and that will help you to be *mechaven* to the essence. You should not really focus on these *kavanos* as their own thing. The best thing, when you *daven*, and in general in life, is to be *mechaven* to G-d simply and straight, like a little kid. The point of learning all this is to help you reveal that type of *emuna* (faith), not to be thinking all these *tachbulos* (schemes), all these calculations.

audio.lecture: 62 - Chap- 30-1 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

sections.title: Three levels of vessels, and why G-d is hidden in the outer one
sections.summary: The vessels have an inside, a middle and an outside, which limit the intellect, the emotions and the action of the light. The word *seser*, hidden, is *rosh toch sof* backwards: the main concealment is in the outer vessel, where a person, and G-d in nature, is seen only by what was done.

phrases.en: there's three levels in the *kelim*:

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: There are three levels in the *kelim* (vessels): the *pnimiyus*, the *emtzaiyus* and the *chitzoniyus*, the inner, the middle and the outer. The idea is known: corresponding to the three groups of three *sefiros*, the three triads of *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi*, that is, the *sechel* (intellect), the emotions, and the impulse to act upon the emotion, there are three types of vessels. The inner vessels limit the light of the intellect, the *Chabad* within the light. The middle vessels limit the emotions of the light. And the external vessels limit and bring out the *Nehi*, **the external expression of the light**.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

phrases.en: and this is what it says, that You, *Hashem*, are hidden.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

phrases.he: שעיקר ההגבלה וההסתר בחיצוניות הכלים כו'
phrases.en: because the main limitation and the main concealment is in the *chitzoniyus* of the *kelim*, the external vessels, which is the *sof*.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: This is what it says, *atah seser*: You, G-d, are hidden. Look at the word *seser*: its letters, *samech*, *tav*, *reish*, are backwards. Read the other way they are *reish*, *tav*, *samech*, the initials of *rosh toch sof* (head, middle and end). For the idea of something hidden, something covered, is that the inside is hidden in the middle, and the middle is hidden in the outside. **The main limitation and the main concealment is in the *chitzoniyus* of the *kelim***, the external vessels, which are the *sof*.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.title: Seeing only what a person did
blocks.text: Why? When a person does something or says something, the main thing you see is the external thing he did. Usually you do not even see how he feels about it, to appreciate why he is doing it. If you could see how he feels, if you could put yourself in his shoes a little, you would understand better what he is doing. And if you could understand how he looks at things, if you could get into his actual mind, you would understand him even more. But when a person's expression comes into his body and out through the external vessels, it is very hidden. You do not see the intellect and emotions anymore, why he is doing it or how he feels; you just see what happened. The revelation of the person is very hidden there.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text:
It is the same with G-d and the world. When G-d runs the world through the external vessels, setting up a system of *teva* (nature), the sun giving us light, which is an external vessel for our *parnasa* (livelihood), the wheat He makes grow and that we make into bread, an external vessel for our food and energy, then G-dliness is very hidden. We are able to say, "Oh look, I don't need G-d, I have my wheat."

With the *mon* (manna) they felt the dependence more, because it came only every day, and they had nothing saved up. But when a person has something saved up, it is very easy for him to think, "Oh, what can G-d do to me? I have all this wheat saved up in my silo. My storehouses are full of wheat." He thinks he is set, and he does not really feel his dependence on G-d anymore. And all that is when it comes to the external vessel.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Already in the middle vessel, like *chesed*, which is what creates everything from nothing, you see that it must come from somewhere. The main thing that covers over G-dliness is that people say, "Oh, it's Mother Nature," like the scientists say, "Oh look, it's a scientific thing, it's not from G-d." Really, the system of *teva* is also from G-d, but they do not see that.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: But when it comes to where the world originally came from, there they cannot hide it. They cannot ignore that G-d must have created the world. All they can do is say, "Well, it was a really long time ago, Big Bang, we don't know how it happened. We know what happened after that, but we don't know how that started." And really they are not even so sure about what happened after that. But when it comes to an external vessel like that, it is much more hidden.

sections.title: Vessels that reveal to oneself, and vessels that bring it out to others
sections.summary: A vessel reveals the light to oneself, as the brain, heart and liver do; the *tikunim* bring it out to someone else. These too have an inner, middle and outer level, for intellect, emotion and deed.

phrases.he: וגם בענין מה שיש בכלי בחינת השפעת וירידת השפע למקבל דוקא כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: also in the *inyan* of the *kelim* that they bring the *or* down to a *mekabel*,

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

phrases.en: So this *inyan* of the *kelim* also has three levels: the inner, the middle, and the external *kli*.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: The vessels also bring the light down to a *mekabel* (receiver). As explained before, there are two *inyanim* (matters) of a vessel: *kelim* and *tikunim*. The matter of a *kli* as such is just to reveal the light to yourself.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Your brain is a vessel for your soul to reveal its intellect to itself: when an idea comes into your brain, you know clearly what you are thinking. Your heart is a vessel to reveal your emotions to yourself, so that you know what you are feeling, because it changes the way your heart beats and your lungs breathe. And your liver, the whole digestive system, is a vessel for you to have physical life and consciousness, so that your soul can relate to the physical world.

audio.lecture: 63 - Chap- 30-2 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: Then there are the vessels to bring it out: not only to reveal it to you in a physical, limited way, but to relate to the outside world. When your soul comes into your brain, you can explain an idea to somebody. When it comes into your heart, you can express the emotion to somebody, because it is from your heart that you will want to do things for him. And through your liver you have the *koach hamaaseh* (the power of action) to do it. These are the external vessels, called *tikunim*. And this matter of the vessels also has three levels: the inner, the middle and the external vessel.

That is in the right side of the heart, which is lit from the brain of *chachma*, because **the brain rules over the heart**. Your brain tells your heart what emotion to have.

blocks.title: He hit me
blocks.text: If somebody did something nice to you, you say, "Oh, that was so nice. I like this person." That is what your brain says to you, and then your heart says, "Ah, I like," and it feels like love. And if somebody hit you, your brain says, "Oh, look what that guy did! He hit me." It thinks about it and says, "Oh, I hate him. I want to get him." And then it shines in your heart as anger, or as fear if he is bigger than you and you don't think you can get him.

audio.lecture: 64 - Chap- 30-3 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: This is mainly through the nerves. The nerves are like the *Chabad*. The nerves that go from the brain to the heart connect to the right side of the heart and control how fast it beats. That is the *Chabad* of the *midda*: the part of the brain that connects to the emotions goes through the nerves and connects to the brain of the heart, the nerves around the heart. The right side of the heart is the part connected to the nerves, and that is what decides how fast the heart will beat: "I think it's called the sinus node, something like that." So that is the inner vessel of the heart, where it connects to the intellect.

The feeling of love is relaxed, calm; the whole body gets calm. The heart could beat faster, but usually it beats slowly, the breathing is slow, "ah": that is usually *ahava* (love). *Yira*, fear or anger, usually makes the heart beat very quickly, and everything gets tense. There is a different feeling for each emotion in your heart, your lungs, your breathing and heartbeat, even your whole body, and from these different patterns you know what emotion you are feeling. That is the difference between the emotions.

blocks.text: The external part of the heart is the lungs, **the vessel for the sinking in of the emotions, the effect it has on your body**. It corresponds to *nefesh*, the *Nehi* of the emotions, their practical ability. This is mainly connected to the oxygen your lungs put into your blood, because it is very important to have a lot of oxygen for the power of action, for your muscles to be able to work. If a person is scared and his body says he is going to need to run or fight, it puts a lot of oxygen into the blood. That is one of the reasons a person starts to breathe faster and the heart beats faster: to get more blood and oxygen to the body and get it ready for action.

blocks.text: It comes from the leftovers in the blood: all the leftover chemicals, messages and hormones put into the blood by the middle vessel, the felt level of the emotions, as was said before. All those chemical traces are left in the blood, and they tell the liver what to do and how to react. If a person is scared, for example, it tells the liver to stop the digestion for a while. That is why a person's stomach drops when he is nervous or scared: if you are going to fight, it is better to have all the energy for your muscles and not to be digesting. And if you are calm and happy, you digest more, because you feel it is safe to spend the energy digesting the food. That is the *mochin*, the *Chabad*, of the liver.

audio.lecture: 65 - Chap- 30-4 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim.mp3

blocks.text: This is also the source of dreams, as it will say. All these leftover letters, chemical letters in the blood, trigger different associations when they go to the brain, and that causes imaginations. It goes into the liver, gets mixed up with the blood and with the food you ate, the liver switches around the order of everything, and it goes back up to the brain. So it creates a kind of chemical static in your blood, and at night, when you are sleeping and your brain is not so active, it picks up these little signals, and they cause your dreams.

blocks.text: In general, these are the *kavana*, the *bracha* (blessing) and the *maaseh* (action), which are like thought, speech and action. They are also called *yichud*, *bracha*, *kedusha*: the *yichud* you make, the *bracha*, and the *kedusha*, the holiness. The point of a *bracha* is to verbalize your feelings to G-d, to say thank you, and saying it also helps you to feel it. Either way, speech is mainly to express emotion and to help you feel it. That is why the *bracha* refers to emotion: speech is the vessel to express the emotion, and speech also helps bring it out. These three, *yichud*, *bracha*, *kedusha*, are called *Yabok*, which is the name of a river.

The more that general *gilui Elokus* and *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) to G-d are strengthened, the more all the *mitzvos* grow. sections.title: Why a vessel without the light is a body without a soul
sections.summary: Even with a root of their own, the brain, heart and liver need the light of the *Kav* to reveal G-d, as a body shows its life by moving. And since the whole purpose of a vessel is to bring out the light, without it the vessel is a body without a soul: it does not spread or grow.

blocks.text: True, the vessels have their own source, so they are able to exist without the shining of the *Kav*. So too the names, the vessels: even if they exist, they need the *Kav* to really reveal G-d, so that you see that they are controlled by G-d according to His *ratzon* (will), that He has *bechira* and is choosing how they should go.

blocks.question: If the vessels have their own source, higher than the lights, why make a big fuss about what is not the main thing, and say that without the light they are like a body without a soul?
blocks.text: The main thing of the vessels is that they are meant to correspond to the nine *sefiros* of *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*; that is their whole purpose. The whole purpose of the brain, for example, is to express the *neshama*, to express intellect; the purpose of the heart is mainly to express emotions, and of the liver mainly to express the physical life. If the light is not there, there is no purpose in the vessel.

audio.lecture: 66 - Chap- 30-5 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim (End).mp3

blocks.text: And if the light is increasing, that will automatically cause the vessel to increase. Why? Because the vessel wants to bring over the light, and if you want to bring over a greater light, you make the vessel greater, **in order to bring the light out below**. The whole purpose of the vessel is to bring out the light.

audio.lecture: 66 - Chap- 30-5 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim (End).mp3

blocks.text: So if the light leaves the vessel, **then the vessel is left like a body without a soul**: it will not spread out, it will not grow or develop any further, and you will not see any life in it now either. The whole purpose of the vessel is to reveal G-dliness, and if that is not being revealed in it, it has no purpose. Then G-d's *ratzon* no longer goes into it to keep it growing and animated. And that is enough to understand.

audio.lecture: 66 - Chap- 30-5 Pnimius Emztous and Chitzonius of Keilim (End).mp3
